verification_report.summary:
The supplied proof passes sequential verification relative to the expressly accepted internal inputs. The normalized positive regularization is admissible, and continuity of the smooth semipositive determinant density gives the trace limit for p=f^(1/n) in L1. The all-Ln Gauduchon supremum formula gives the exact right-hand mass without a root-tail hypothesis; Stokes then turns the positive trace inequality into equality. Off the analytic degeneracy locus, local all-Hermitian tests and matrix AM-GM identify the full current with a conformal smooth-root form before any nonlinear product is invoked. The local conformal-current lemma then gives smoothness and the exact equation; both sides vanish on the pluripolar locus, giving the global extended equation and finite mass.

For two threshold subsolutions the difference current is real, closed, order zero, and hence normal. Demailly's support theorems apply without positivity: on the divisorial regular locus they give the component coefficients, and Corollary 2.11 kills the residual codimension-at-least-two support. The real coefficients have the stated smooth Bott--Chern relation. The book normalization ddc=i/(2pi) partial-barpartial recovers each coefficient as the generic Lelong-number difference. The stated local multiplier-ideal criterion then proves uniqueness within an I-equivalence class, ordinary equivalence implies I-equivalence, and linear independence (including the absence of divisors when codim Z>=2) gives type-free uniqueness.

The required arXiv-first theorem query encountered an SSL transport error. The prescribed web fallback verified the cited statements and hypotheses in Demailly's official 21 June 2012 CADG PDF, Chapter III Corollaries 2.11 and 2.14 (printed pp.141 and 143). The draft correctly assumes, rather than asserts generally, smooth semipositive attainment; it makes no root-tail, BMP, lower-mass, singular-current wedge, or novelty claim.
